sections.html:
• Scientific name: Pseudomugil gertrudae
  • Common names: Gertrude's Spotted Blue Eye, Spotted Blue Eye Rainbowfish, Gertrudae Rainbowfish
  • Temperament: Peaceful
  • Adult size: approximately 2.5–4 cm (1–1.5 inches)
Native to the slow-moving waters and wetlands of northern Australia and New Guinea.
Tank size: 10 gallons (about 40 litres) or larger. Keep them in groups of at least 6–8 individuals to encourage natural schooling behaviour and male display activity.

• Temperature: 23–28°C (74–82°F)
  • pH: 6.0–7.5
  • Water flow: gentle to moderate

They appreciate stable water quality and mature aquariums with plenty of plant cover.

They thrive in heavily planted aquariums with:

  • Dense aquatic plants
  • Floating plants for cover
  • Dark substrate
  • Open swimming areas
  • Stable water conditions

Their colours become especially vibrant under natural-style lighting and planted aquascapes.

Omnivorous nano fish that readily accept:

  • High-quality micro pellets
  • Crushed flakes
  • Baby brine shrimp
  • Daphnia
  • Frozen cyclops
  • Small live foods

A varied diet helps maximise coloration and breeding behaviour.

Peaceful, active mid-to-top water swimmers that school. Males display vibrant finnage and flashing behaviour when competing for attention. Compatible tank mates include small rasboras, Corydoras, peaceful shrimp, kuhli loaches, small tetras and other nano rainbowfish. Avoid aggressive or fin-nipping fish; due to their small size they should not be housed with large or aggressive fish.
